15:46 local, 19:46 GMT, 01:16 IST: Just eight balls into the final session, Jayden Seales wraps things up with the final wicket to complete a deserved five-wicket haul as West Indies seal a commanding victory to take 1-0 lead. It is a win built on seizing the key moments across all four innings. Kavem Hodge's gritty 84 and Shai Hope's fluent 92 provided the backbone with the bat, while Pakistan's reply was shaped by Shan Masood's superb century before Shamar Joseph's dismissal of Salman Agha sparked a dramatic collapse. Justin Greaves then turned the game on its head with a stunning spell of five successive wicket maidens, claiming his maiden Test five-for and handing West Indies a tiny yet crucial first-innings lead.

Pakistan fought back through Mohammad Abbas' outstanding five-wicket haul to keep the chase within touching distance, but the final innings belonged to the West Indies quicks once again. Jayden Seales ripped through the top order, Babar Azam stood tall with the only substantial resistance, and the rest never found enough support as the target proved a bridge too far. Fittingly, Seales claimed the last wicket as well. It is only West Indies' second win in their last 11 Tests, while Pakistan's eighth successive away Test defeat - their longest such streak, stretching back to their last overseas win in Sri Lanka in July 2023. Stick around for the post-match reactions...

That brings the curtain down on a memorable first-ever Test at the Brian Lara Stadium. It had a bit of everything - rain interruptions on the opening day, Shan Masood's fighting hundred, Kavem Hodge and Shai Hope's resilience, Mohammad Abbas' superb five-for, Justin Greaves' historic spell of five successive wicket maidens and Jayden Seales' match-winning five-for. Fittingly, all 40 wickets in the match fell to pace, underlining just how much assistance the seamers extracted from the surface over four days. The action now shifts to the historic Queen's Park Oval in Port of Spain, Trinidad, where the second and final Test begins on August 2. The visitors will be desperate to snap their longest-ever overseas losing streak, while West Indies will look to wrap up the series. And perhaps there couldn't have been a more fitting tribute on Sir Garfield Sobers' birth anniversary, with captain Roston Chase dedicating this memorable victory to the great man. Until next time, it's goodbye from all of us.
